M1.label: verified
M1.text: `get` takes `mu_` with a `lock_guard` before it reads `map_`.

M2.label: verified
M2.text: `resolve` calls `slow_lookup` between `cache_.get` and `cache_.put`, and holds no lock there.

M3.label: inferred
M3.text: Two threads can both miss in `get` before either calls `put`, so both call `slow_lookup`.
M3.why: get() releases mu_ at its closing brace before resolve() reaches slow_lookup, so nothing orders the two threads' checks against each other's stores.

M4.label: verified
M4.text: In the coarse variant `slow_lookup` is called while the `lock_guard` on `mu_` is still alive.

M5.label: inferred
M5.text: A caller of a different key also waits for `mu_` during that lookup.
M5.why: mu_ guards the whole map, not one key.

M6.label: verified
M6.text: A caller that finds an `inflight_` entry copies its future and waits in `future.get` outside the lock.
